headline: Learned molecular representations drive deep models of drug-target and binding affinity
label: Deep Learning Molecular Interaction Prediction
summary: Recent 2026 preprints and papers extend interaction prediction with physics priors, contrastive embeddings and multimodal fusion.
synthesis: The dominant thread is deep learning that pairs learned molecular or protein representations with graph or sequence encoders for interaction and property prediction. MMU-DPI fuses MPNN, CNN and GAT branches with a label-space Label Mix strategy, while GAPEK uses ESM-2 and Mole-BERT embeddings to predict kcat, Km and Ki. Data scarcity recurs: CheMeleon pretrains a ~10M-parameter model on calculable descriptors for low-data regimes. Physics-based priors appear in structure-based affinity models via mtenn and in Dual-State Query, which embeds the MWC allostery model for GPCR bioactivity. The BCL-2 study differs, combining diffusion-based complex generation for 3094 FDA drugs with trajectory analysis and in vitro validation of Relugolix. The novelty lies in descriptor-based pretraining, label-space regularization and physics-embedded architectures rather than in any single backbone.
